title: A Cropping Calendar That Dates Every Task From Day Zero
metaTitle: Cropping Calendar App: Plan Every Farm Task by Day Count
metaDescription: A cropping calendar for Filipino farms: land preparation to harvest, every task dated by DAS, DAT or DAP from each lot's day zero. Start free on anee.io.
excerpt: The anee.io cropping calendar holds your whole season on one board, from land preparation to harvest. It dates every task from each lot's own day zero, so a lot sown a week late keeps its own timing. When the weather moves your plan, you drag the task and the calendar follows.

blocks.text: What goes on your cropping calendar

In anee.io a season lives in a cropping schedule, and the Activities board is its calendar. Each day is a card. Open it to see what happens that day, on which lot, who works it and what it costs. The day card also shows each lot's growth stage, so you know what the crop is doing while you plan.

items: Tasks: land preparation, sowing, transplanting, fertilizer, spraying, weeding and harvest
Irrigation days, placed by crop stage
Hired services like the tractor, the harvester or the thresher, with their cost
Payroll days for your [workers and their pay](/features/farm-workers-and-payroll), on Solo Farmer and Farm Owner
Reminders and checklists for the small things that slip
Day notes with photos and voice notes, plus video clips on Solo Farmer and Farm Owner

blocks.text: Day zero and the DAS, DAT or DAP count

Farmers count days after an event, not calendar dates. Rice recommendations from PhilRice speak of days after sowing or transplanting, and the board works the same way.

Each lot has its own day zero. For direct seeded palay (rice still in the husk) it is the sowing date, and the count is DAS, days after sowing. Transplanted rice counts DAS in the seedbed, then DAT from the day you transplant. For corn and many vegetables the count is DAP, days after planting. Every task shows its count beside the date, so 'DAT 21' and the weekday sit together on one card.

Need the usual timings? Our guide to [pagtatanim ng palay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-palay) walks through the rice season, and [fertilizer for rice](/blog/fertilizer-for-rice) lists when each application usually goes in. Put those days on your board once and they stay dated for every lot.

blocks.text: When the season does not follow the plan

Rain comes early, the tractor is late, a typhoon closes the road for three days. On the board you drag a task to its new day, or move a whole day's work at once to a new date or day number. Keep an idea you have not decided on as a draft. Save a version of the plan when you want to try another timing without losing the original.

You can undo any change, even after you log out and come back tomorrow. That works because anee.io keeps the steps on the server, not only on your phone.

If a lot runs behind, set its delay counter. Each task then shows the delayed count beside the calendar's count, so you see where the crop really stands.

Tag tasks by input, by lot or by anything your farm uses. Then filter the board to show only what you need today, like the whole day labor or every herbicide spray. Search finds one task by name when the season gets long.
Take the cropping calendar to the field

anee.io is a web app that runs in any phone browser, so the board goes wherever you go. On the Solo Farmer and Farm Owner plans, offline mode keeps your recent seasons on the phone. Tick tasks done, move dates, write day notes and take photos where there is no signal. Your changes sync when the connection comes back.

Workers can follow the board too. On the Farm Owner plan each worker gets a login, and you decide if they may view or edit the plan.

items.a: It is the season's plan laid out by date: when to prepare the land, sow, fertilize, spray, irrigate and harvest. In anee.io each task also carries its day count from the lot's day zero.

items.q: What do DAS, DAT and DAP mean?
items.a: Days after sowing, days after transplanting and days after planting. Each lot uses the count that fits how you planted it, and the board shows it on every task.

items.q: Can two lots follow different dates?
items.a: Yes. Each lot has its own day zero, so a lot planted a week later keeps its own timing on the same board.
